title: The AI boom needs power and rockets. Trump just exempted both from environmental law.
excerpt: The Trump administration spent Tuesday clearing environmental law out of the way of the tech boom. It did so twice, on two fronts, with the same justification. content_html:
The Trump administration spent Tuesday clearing environmental law out of the way of the tech boom. It did so twice, on two fronts, with the same justification.

The first move exempts data centres from the rules meant to stop acid rain. The second frees rocket launches from federal environmental review. Together they show how far the government will bend its own rulebook to speed up the physical infrastructure behind AI and space.

Data centres, off the acid-rain books

The Environmental Protection Agency has pulled data-centre power plants out of the Clean Air Act’s Acid Rain Program, Engadget reported, citing Reuters. The exemption covers “islanded” plants that feed a data centre rather than the public grid.

Freed from the programme, they no longer have to cut emissions of sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, the gases behind acid rain. Nearly 60 such plants are already running or being built, most of them fast-tracked.

The EPA’s logic is narrow. The Acid Rain Program covers electric utilities. A plant wired to a single data centre is not a utility, because it serves no public customers. Aaron Szabo, its assistant administrator for air, framed the exemption in national terms.

“Ensuring that the United States maintains our artificial intelligence dominance is essential to national security and economic prosperity,” he said. The agency called it a “commonsense” approach to regulating.

The scale is the problem. Bloomberg projects data centres will draw a fifth of America’s electricity within about eight years. Acid rain strips nutrients from soil, poisons lakes and rivers, and damages crops. The precursor gases also worsen asthma and heart conditions in people nearby. That is not a fringe reading. It comes from the EPA’s own website.

Rockets, off the review list

The second move came from the Federal Aviation Administration. It proposed waiving environmental reviews for commercial rocket sites, launches and reentries, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The agency is bracing for a surge, from 214 launches and reentries this fiscal year to more than 500 within a decade. That growth is driven by SpaceX, Blue Origin, Rocket Lab and Stoke Space.

Launches are not quiet neighbours. They generate noise, alter wildlife habitats and reshape the land around them, which is why the reviews exist. Companies counter that the reviews drag on for more than a year and stall their projects. SpaceX has called the analysis of its Starbase site in Texas “superfluous”, even as nearby residents argued the reviews were not thorough enough.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the plan would “supercharge commercial space activity”, CNBC reported. It follows an FCC move last week to loosen how it licenses satellites.

The same argument, twice

The through-line is the framing. In both cases, the case for stripping a rule is national competitiveness, in AI or in space. In both cases, the objection comes from the people living next to the infrastructure. It fits a wider deregulatory push around the buildout.

The administration has already defended xAI’s gas turbines in Memphis, and told towns fighting data centres to give up. “You can’t fight it,” President Trump told them recently. “You have to go with it.”

What communities lose is the paperwork that lets them see what is coming. Environmental reviews and emissions caps are slow. They are also how a town learns what a nearby plant will emit, or what a launch pad will do to its coast. Strip them away and the buildout moves faster, while the bills and the fallout land on the people least able to opt out.

content_html_zh:
特朗普政府周二花了很多时间清理环境法，使其不再阻碍科技繁荣。 它在两个方面这样做了两次，理由相同。

第一步举措使数据中心免受旨在阻止酸雨的规则的约束。 第二项法案使火箭发射免受联邦环境审查。 它们共同展示了政府将在多大程度上改变自己的规则手册，以加快人工智能和太空背后的物理基础设施的建设。

数据中心，远离酸雨书籍

据 Engadget 援引路透社报道，美国环境保护局已将数据中心发电厂从《清洁空气法》的酸雨计划中撤出。 该豁免涵盖为数据中心而不是公共电网供电的“孤岛”工厂。

摆脱该计划后，他们不再需要减少二氧化硫和氮氧化物（酸雨背后的气体）的排放。 近 60 座此类工厂已在运行或正在建设中，其中大多数都在快速推进中。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

EPA 的逻辑是狭隘的。 酸雨计划涵盖电力设施。 连接到单个数据中心的工厂不是公用事业，因为它不为公共客户提供服务。 其航空部门助理局长亚伦·萨博 (Aaron Szabo) 从国家层面制定了豁免规定。

“确保美国保持人工智能的主导地位对于国家安全和经济繁荣至关重要，”他说。 该机构称其为“常识性”监管方法。

规模就是问题。 彭博社预计，数据中心将在大约八年内消耗美国五分之一的电力。 酸雨会夺走土壤中的养分，毒害湖泊和河流，并损害农作物。 这些前体气体还会加剧附近人们的哮喘和心脏病。 这不是边缘读物。 它来自 EPA 自己的网站。

火箭队，脱离评论名单

第二个举措来自美国联邦航空管理局。 据《华尔街日报》报道，它提议放弃对商业火箭场地、发射和重返大气层的环境审查。

该机构正准备迎接激增的发射和重新进入，从本财年的 214 次发射和重新进入，到十年内的 500 多次。 这一增长是由 SpaceX、Blue Origin、Rocket Lab 和 Stoke Space 推动的。

新产品并不是安静的邻居。 它们产生噪音、改变野生动物栖息地并重塑周围的土地，这就是这些评论存在的原因。 公司反驳说，审查拖延了一年多，导致他们的项目陷入停滞。 SpaceX 称对其位于德克萨斯州 Starbase 站点的分析是“多余的”，尽管附近的居民认为这些审查不够彻底。

据 CNBC 报道，交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 表示，该计划将“促进商业太空活动”。 此前，美国联邦通信委员会上周采取了放宽卫星许可方式的举措。

同样的论点，两次

贯穿线就是框架。 在这两种情况下，废除规则的理由都是国家竞争力，无论是在人工智能还是在太空方面。 在这两种情况下，反对意见都来自居住在基础设施附近的人们。 它适合围绕扩建进行更广泛的放松管制的推动。

政府已经为 xAI 在孟菲斯的燃气轮机辩护，并告诉与数据中心作战的城镇放弃。 “你无法与之抗争，”特朗普总统最近告诉他们。 “你必须接受它。”

社区失去的是让他们了解即将发生的事情的文书工作。 环境审查和排放上限进展缓慢。 它们也是城镇了解附近工厂将排放什么，或者发射台将对其海岸造成什么影响的方式。 如果把它们去掉，扩建就会加快，而账单和后果就会落在那些最无力选择退出的人身上。
